A1 and A2 milk differ in their beta-casein protein composition. A1 milk contains both A1 and A2 beta-casein, while A2 milk contains only the A2 variant. Some people experience better digestion with A2 milk, as the A1 beta-casein may break down into a peptide (BCM-7) that can cause digestive discomfort in some individuals. 
A1 Milk:
Contains: Primarily A1 beta-casein, but also contains A2 beta-casein. 
Digestion: Some people find A1 milk more difficult to digest, possibly due to the BCM-7 peptide. 
Source: Typically comes from cow breeds like Holstein, Friesian, and British Shorthorn. 
A2 Milk:
Contains: Only A2 beta-casein protein.
Digestion: Some people find A2 milk easier to digest than A1 milk.
Source: Often produced by breeds like Jersey, Guernsey, Charolais, and Limousin.
